questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: It was obligatory. but I would probably have chosen to go on exchange even if it wasn't. I would want to do it for the experiences, networking and learning.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I had to choose Korea (as I study korean studies), I chose the university for a variety of reasons. I chose a school that didn't have a language school, so I could take subjects in Korean. I wanted to go outside of Seoul - in hope of speaking more Korean than english. And I chose a university in Daegu, because it's still a big city, with many opportunities and experiences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing experience. It was fun and I learned a lot!! The only thing that wasn't great was that the subjects I ended up taking, wasn't the most interesting, but that was my mistake.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: generally it was okay and when it was difficult there were many other exchange students who were just as confused as me, so we could figure it out together.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction meeting, we received printed out information, there was an international office - with student helpers, we received a buddy from the school to help us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: the dormitory information was very lacking and all information once you moved in was only in Korean.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are many dorms on campus, but the school had one specific dorm to foreign exchange students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
No 'real' cooking facilities - there were a shared fridge and microwaves. For meal plans, there was a cafeteria at the dorm (the food wasn't the best, but it was convenient). You could choose 0, 1, 1.5, 2,  or 3 meals per day. There was also a convenience store and a coffee shop at the dormitory. 

There was other eating facilities and cafeterias at campus (some was quite nice)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
They should be aware that the workers at the dorm doesn't necessarily speak english and information over the announcement system is all in Korean. 
I would also clean it before moving in. When moving out, all you have to do is show pictures of the room, and the staff does not check in person, so the room can be quite gross. 

also, there is a curfew from between 1am to 5am, so you receive penalty points if you come home between 1-5. If you get to many penalty points they might throw you out of the dorm.

questions.answer: i don't really remember.... sorry

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't think I received help with the application process. But after I started at the school, there was a few people we could email for help and they replied quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty unsuccesful... Because my study in UCPH didn't align with a major they had, so I was assigned to a major that didn't allow me to take the subject I wanted when the application process started. I had to wait about 3 hours for application to open up for subjects outside of your major.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some subject I had was interesting others weren't

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It really depends. I took to Korean lesson - those were a pretty high level. I took a subject with Korean students - which wasn't to wasy or to difficult. and then lastly I chose a subject meant for foreigners about modern korean society - it was very easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is not very engaging. You sit and listen for the most part and have homework. there is not a lot of class discussion. I found myself loosing concentration a lot...

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Modern Korean society, Modern Korea in international history, Practical Korean listening, Academic Korean reading.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to look beyond the list given to exhange students. I found my subject 'modern Korea in international history' on the universities website (where you can find many subjects beyond the list provided)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to go to the doctors (it was pretty cheap though)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things are pretty cheap in Korea, but fruit & vegetables are very expensive. It is very cheap to eat Korean food, but international food tends to be more expensive in comparison. Transportation and entreence fees are very reasonable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was a gym you could join for a small fee. They had many clubs (including sports), but not all allowed foreigners to join. The had every club you could think of. 
I joined a culture & language exchange club. it was a lot of fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend joining a club - I met a lot of new friends and had a lot of fun in the club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Daegu, is a very easy city to travel from and there are many exciting places to see nearby. Specifically I recommend Gyeongju (which is only 15 minutes away with the KTX). 
There is a lot of beautiful nature in Daegu, I would recommend to go see it. Also the local amusement park is surprisingly fun.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Surprisingly easy. I had an open-mind and did not say no to new experiences - it made it very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Korean people can be a little shy on the first meeting, but they are kind and helpful. you just have to be the one to engage in the beginning. 
Also just in general. the first few weeks, try to say yes to all social event (big and small) it's easier to make friends before friend groups are established. Even though it might be exhausting the first few weeks.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
I really missed good bread and salty food. 
I didn't find the cultural differences to bad - but I had also researched a bit before leaving, so I had an idea of what to expect.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food was delicious, the people were kind, the nature was beautiful and there was always something fun to do.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be outgoing and meet people from both Korea and all over the world. Don't just stay around Campus, but take advantage of all the opportunities around. The University itself also provides experiences for echange student. A city tour, a trip to another city, festivals, the 'social hour' event and much more.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I feel like I might just repeat myself...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The many friends I made was the best part.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes I would be a little language confused. Living at a dorm for foreingers,, you heard a lot of different languages and sometimes when I was tired, it became difficult to communicate.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
